title: Fifteen Minutes Before Closing
summary: A closing-time diary about compressed attention, last looks, and the strange focus that comes with limited time.
main_text:
The final fifteen minutes of a museum visit often produce the sharpest looking. With closing time announced and the rooms beginning to thin, every decision becomes clearer: one last return to a favorite wall, one final pause in front of a work that resisted understanding, one fast glance at the pieces you know you will not carry home.

That pressure can cheapen a visit, but today it clarified it. I stopped trying to see everything fairly and instead let instinct lead. The works that mattered most were the ones I turned back toward without argument. They had already done their work on me earlier in the day; the final minutes only made that fact visible.

Leaving a gallery at closing is always slightly unfinished, and maybe that is right. Art should not resolve neatly just because the lights are dimming. A good visit ends with something still unsettled enough to follow you outside.
